title: The fireworks, ordered
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The uncle orders the Fourth's fireworks from a catalog the way he has since '71. A form. His hand. Gully fills it; the uncle signs. Same as the permit. The strip notices the signature is worse than February's and doesn't say so.

panels.composition: The shack. A fireworks catalog, garish, drawn gray. GULLY filling an order form at the counter. The UNCLE in the chair. WOOD.

image.prompt: a teenager filling in an order form from a fireworks catalog at a bait shack counter while an old man watches from a lawn chair, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The catalog page: bursts, drawn as white on black. The uncle's finger on one.

image.prompt: close on a fireworks catalog page with bursts rendered white on black and an old finger pointing at one, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle signing. Slower than February. The line wandering more. The strip draws it exactly and says nothing.

image.prompt: close on an old man's hand signing a form with a slow wandering line, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The form in an envelope. Gully licking it. The uncle looking at the bay. 'Red ones,' he says, to nobody. The strip can't do red.

image.prompt: a teenager sealing an envelope while an old man in a lawn chair looks out at the bay, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Red ones.' Since '71. The signature, worse; the strip says nothing.
